argument:
The bull's 7% underlying revenue growth, 14% EBITDA growth and 22% H1 ex-exceptional profit growth demonstrate real hospital improvement. Positive cash after the conservative financing bridge also means costs did not consume all period cash. These observations justify a growth thesis independently of accounting inflation.

The remaining downside is shareholder conversion at a premium: RM141m post-financing surplus versus RM486m dividends leaves a cash shortfall, while RM11.564bn net debt excludes RM2.205bn leases. Retention or payout adjustment could aid repair, but neither is an observed decision here. Singapore admission weakness and unresolved governance statements further qualify extrapolation without implying adverse legal outcomes. At 30.38x trailing earnings, continued growth offers compensation only if capital demands and payout choices allow it to reach shareholders. I favor measured exposure over treating profitable expansion as already-financial repair.
key_points: Underlying hospital growth survives accounting objections.
Post-financing cash is positive but insufficient for dividends.
Premium valuation and leverage require better shareholder conversion.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers whether the operating engine is improving and avoids defending uncovered payouts. It does not resolve the observed dividend gap; future retained cash could repair it, but is not yet demonstrated.
